mappings.note: Assertion and reason are literally that sexual reproduction creates variation because gamete fusion brings unique chromosome combinations. The single best fit in the whole chapter for the variation outcome; the C-3.2-LO-5 twin is not used because variation is C3.3's subject, not C3.2's.

Orders the steps of artificial hybridisation, all of which are pollination control. Distinguished from the sibling emasculation items only by the task verb (ordering rather than explaining), so this family honestly shares one outcome.
Names P. Maheshwari. LO-12 names him explicitly, so this is the one item in the chapter that fits it exactly. LO-11 rejected: Maheshwari's contribution is plant embryology, not human anatomy.

Why an abiotic agent forces huge pollen output. The agent is the whole explanation, so the seed-dispersal-and-pollination-agents outcome, not C-3.2-LO-4, which would only cover naming the pollination type.

Infers wind versus insect from pollen and stigma traits in a table. Same outcome as the insect-features item; split from it only by which direction the inference runs (traits to agent here, agent to traits there).
How sexual reproduction confers survival advantage through variation. The variation outcome, not LO-9: no asexual mode is put alongside it, so there is nothing being compared.
Egg numbers follow from the mode of fertilisation being external. The fertilisation limb of LO-4; this is the MCQ twin of the short-answer item on the same point in part 1.
Finds the false statement about fertilisation mode and offspring survival; the error is calling frog fertilisation internal. Turns entirely on the mode of fertilisation, so LO-4.
Identifies the Copper-T and its mechanism. Squarely the contraceptive-device limb of LO-10, which is the only limb of that fused row that this item touches.
POOR FIT. Orders the butterfly life cycle. Metamorphosis and post-embryonic development have no outcome anywhere in this chapter's frame; the competency is the ceiling.
POOR FIT. Embryonic nourishment by yolk in birds, mammals, fish. No outcome covers embryonic nutrition. C-3.2-LO-4 rejected because fertilisation is over before the question begins.
POOR FIT. Predicts a larval stage from low yolk content. Same uncovered territory as the other yolk items; nothing in the frame reaches development after fertilisation.

Reads a four-species table and picks the highest survival, which the answer attributes to internal fertilisation plus internal development. The decisive variable is the mode of fertilisation, so LO-4 rather than the uncovered development territory.

Which male structure both makes sperm and secretes pubertal hormones. Answered by naming an organ, so LO-8. The pubertal-hormone clause has no outcome of its own, but it is not what the student must supply.
Scrotum position and why. Describing a male reproductive organ and its functional anatomy, so LO-8. Not C-5.1-LO-1: verbal assertion-reason, no illustration.

POOR FIT. Reads a menstrual-cycle phase table and predicts the consequence of no fertilisation. Cycle physiology has no outcome; C-3.2-LO-4 rejected because the item is about the uterine lining, not about fertilisation itself.
Names the accessory glands of the male tract. LO-8 covers the male reproductive organs; this item is split from the testis item only by which organ is asked for.
Names the oviduct as the passage from ovary to uterus. Female organ identification, so LO-8; the diagram-based version of this same content elsewhere in the chapter takes C-5.1-LO-1 in addition.

Sperm versus egg on size, number, motility and stored nutrients. Mapped to LO-8 as the products of the male and female reproductive organs; this is a mild extension of that outcome's wording, since the frame has no gamete-structure outcome.

Subhash Mukhopadhyay and India's first IVF baby. LO-13 names assisted reproductive technologies exactly; C6.1 carries the Indian-contribution angle. LO-11 deliberately NOT used: it is specific to human anatomy, and IVF is a medical technique, not an anatomical finding.
Orders sperm entry, ascent, fusion, cleavage, implantation. The pivot of the sequence is fertilisation, so LO-4; the frame has no implantation or pregnancy outcome to take the tail of the sequence.
The importance of gametogenesis is chromosome halving. Constancy again, not variation, so not C-3.3-LO-5; no meiosis outcome exists, so the competency.

POOR FIT. Matches the four stages of the 28-day cycle to their events. Cycle physiology, uncovered. One of the nine items in this chapter that land on the competency purely because the menstrual cycle has no outcome.

POOR FIT. Assertion and reason on why the lining sheds when no fertilisation occurs. Mapped to the competency rather than C-3.2-LO-4 because the reasoning being tested is about the uterine lining, not about fertilisation.
POOR FIT. Trimesters and when organogenesis begins. Gestation has no outcome in this frame at all.
